applyTo: "*.md,data/*.md"

# Markdown documentation instructions — Voice360

## Tone and style
- Write for a technical reviewer and a non-technical assessor simultaneously.
- Use short sentences. Avoid passive voice where active is clearer.
- Do not invent metrics, call volumes, cost figures, or satisfaction scores unless a cited dataset exists.
- Do not make coverage, liability, or payment claims on behalf of the fictional insurer.

## Structure conventions
- Top-level heading (`#`) = document title only.
- Second-level (`##`) = major sections.
- Third-level (`###`) = subsections.
- Use tables for structured comparisons, inputs/outputs, and test cases.
- Use fenced code blocks with a language tag for all code, JSON, and expressions.
- Use `mermaid` fenced blocks for flow diagrams.

## Security language rules
- Never include real policy numbers, real dates of birth, real phone numbers, or real names in documentation.
- Demo values must be clearly labeled as fictional: `POL-1001`, `Asha Sharma (fictional)`.
- Do not document internal connector secrets, environment IDs, or SharePoint URLs.

## What not to add
- Do not add a "generated by AI" disclaimer to every file — record AI usage in `10-github-copilot-evidence.md` instead.
- Do not duplicate content already in another numbered document — cross-reference it.
- Do not add emojis to formal documents (`01-` through `11-`).
